Unforgettable Olympic moments.Abebe Bikila runs barefoot: Barefoot on the cobbles of Rome, the Ethiopian marathoner set a world record, then won again in Tokyo in 1964 wearing shoes.
Unforgettable Olympic moments.Black Power salute: Tommie Smith and John Carlos raised gloved fists on the Mexico City podium. Silver medalist Peter Norman of Australia wore a human-rights badge in support.
Unforgettable Olympic moments.Mark Spitz wins 7 golds: Each of Spitz's seven Munich golds came with a world record, and nobody matched the haul until Michael Phelps in 2008.
Unforgettable Olympic moments.Carl Lewis wins 4 golds: Lewis matched Jesse Owens' feat of 1936 by winning the 100 m, 200 m, long jump and 4x100 m relay at Los Angeles.
Unforgettable Olympic moments.Ben Johnson stripped of gold: The Canadian sprinter ran 9.79 s in Seoul but tested positive for stanozolol days later. His gold went to Carl Lewis.
Unforgettable Olympic moments.The Dream Team: The first US Olympic basketball team of NBA pros, with Jordan, Magic and Bird, won Barcelona gold by an average of over 40 points.
Unforgettable Olympic moments.Kerri Strug's vault: Strug landed her second vault on one foot with an injured ankle, helping the US women win their first Olympic team gold.
Unforgettable Olympic moments.Cathy Freeman's 400 m gold: Freeman lit the Sydney cauldron, then won the 400 m wearing a hooded suit and carried both Australian and Aboriginal flags on her lap of honor.
Unforgettable Olympic moments.Phelps wins 8 golds: Phelps took his eighth gold in Beijing in the 100 m butterfly by just 0.01 seconds, a fingertip margin over Milorad Cavic.
Unforgettable Olympic moments.Bolt's third 100 m gold: Bolt became the first sprinter to win the Olympic 100 m three Games running, after Beijing and London, finishing in Rio in 9.81 s.

Tom Hanks films by release.Splash: Hanks plays a man who falls for a mermaid played by Daryl Hannah in this romantic comedy, one of his first big hits.
Tom Hanks films by release.Big: Hanks earned his first Oscar nomination as a boy in a man's body, and the floor-piano scene at FAO Schwarz is famous.
Tom Hanks films by release.Philadelphia: He won his first Best Actor Oscar playing a lawyer with AIDS who sues his own firm, in one of Hollywood's first big films about the epidemic.
Tom Hanks films by release.Forrest Gump: Hanks won his second Best Actor Oscar for this film, back to back, and the film earned about 680 million dollars.
Tom Hanks films by release.Apollo 13: He plays astronaut Jim Lovell, who later had a cameo in the film as the captain of the recovery ship.
Tom Hanks films by release.Saving Private Ryan: Its opening 24 minutes recreate the D-Day landing at Omaha Beach in intense, handheld detail, and it earned Spielberg an Oscar.
Tom Hanks films by release.Cast Away: Production paused for a year while Hanks lost weight and grew a beard to portray years on a desert island with his volleyball Wilson.
Tom Hanks films by release.The Da Vinci Code: Ron Howard's adaptation of Dan Brown's bestseller has Hanks as symbologist Robert Langdon, with scenes shot in the Louvre.
Tom Hanks films by release.Captain Phillips: The film dramatizes the 2009 hijacking of the Maersk Alabama, and Somali newcomer Barkhad Abdi earned an Oscar nomination.
Tom Hanks films by release.Sully: Eastwood's film dramatizes the Hudson River landing, in which pilot Chesley Sullenberger saved all 155 aboard in about a few minutes.

Mughal emperors, by accession.Babur: The Mughal founder, descended from both Timur and Genghis Khan, won at Panipat and wrote a famous memoir, the Baburnama.
Mughal emperors, by accession.Humayun: He lost his throne to Sher Shah Suri, fled to Persia, regained it, and died soon after falling down his library stairs.
Mughal emperors, by accession.Akbar: He expanded the empire, ended a tax on non-Muslims, and held debates among scholars of many faiths.
Mughal emperors, by accession.Jahangir: His powerful wife Nur Jahan had coins struck in her name and effectively ran much of the court.
Mughal emperors, by accession.Shah Jahan: He built the Taj Mahal for his wife Mumtaz Mahal and later spent his last years confined in Agra Fort by his own son.
Mughal emperors, by accession.Aurangzeb: He ruled nearly 50 years and took the empire to its greatest extent, but costly wars in the Deccan drained its treasury.
Mughal emperors, by accession.Bahadur Shah I: He won a war of succession against his brothers but ruled only about five years, and the empire had already begun to splinter.
Mughal emperors, by accession.Muhammad Shah: Under him, Nader Shah of Persia sacked Delhi in 1739 and carried off the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor diamond.
Mughal emperors, by accession.Shah Alam II: A figurehead for most of his reign, he gave the British East India Company the right to collect Bengal's revenues in 1765.
Mughal emperors, by accession.Bahadur Shah Zafar: The last Mughal emperor was also an Urdu poet; after the 1857 revolt the British exiled him to Rangoon.

Voice assistants and AI models.Siri: It grew from a project at SRI International, was bought by Apple in 2010, and debuted on the iPhone 4S.
Voice assistants and AI models.Google Now: It showed predictive information on cards, such as traffic and flights, before you asked, and was the forerunner of Assistant.
Voice assistants and AI models.Amazon Alexa: Its name was reportedly inspired partly by the ancient Library of Alexandria, and it first lived in the Echo speaker.
Voice assistants and AI models.Google Assistant: It debuted in a chat app called Allo and in Google Home, replacing Google Now.
Voice assistants and AI models.Samsung Bixby: It arrived with the Galaxy S8 and even had its own dedicated button.
Voice assistants and AI models.GPT-2: OpenAI first held back the full model, saying it might be misused to produce fake text.
Voice assistants and AI models.DALL-E: The name mixes the artist Salvador Dali with Pixar's robot WALL-E.
Voice assistants and AI models.ChatGPT: It reached a million users within five days of launching in late 2022.
Voice assistants and AI models.GPT-4: It was the first model from OpenAI to accept images as well as text, and it passed a simulated bar exam.
Voice assistants and AI models.Sora: This text-to-video model was unveiled in early 2024; its name is Japanese for sky.

One 1980s hit per year: put them in orde.The Empire Strikes Back: The Empire Strikes Back reveals the line 'I am your father', and the filming kept the line secret from nearly everyone, including actor Mark Hamill.
One 1980s hit per year: put them in orde.Raiders of the Lost Ark: Raiders of the Lost Ark introduced Indiana Jones, and the giant boulder in the opening was made of fiberglass and plaster.
One 1980s hit per year: put them in orde.E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial: E.T. had its creature built by Carlo Rambaldi, and its face was in part based on faces of Albert Einstein and Ernest Hemingway.
One 1980s hit per year: put them in orde.Return of the Jedi: Return of the Jedi featured the Ewoks and a speeder bike chase filmed in a California redwood forest.
One 1980s hit per year: put them in orde.Ghostbusters: Ghostbusters made a lot of money, and the Ecto-1 was a converted 1959 Cadillac ambulance-hearse.
One 1980s hit per year: put them in orde.Back to the Future: Back to the Future cast Michael J. Fox only after Eric Stoltz had begun filming, and the DeLorean time machine was chosen for its look.
One 1980s hit per year: put them in orde.Top Gun: Top Gun made Navy recruitment soar, and its soundtrack included 'Danger Zone' by Kenny Loggins.
One 1980s hit per year: put them in orde.Dirty Dancing: Dirty Dancing was a low-budget movie, and its famous lift was rehearsed for hours in a lake.
One 1980s hit per year: put them in orde.Who Framed Roger Rabbit: Who Framed Roger Rabbit combined live action with cartoon characters from rival studios, with Disney and Warner characters on screen together.
One 1980s hit per year: put them in orde.Batman (Keaton): Batman starred Michael Keaton, and its Prince-written soundtrack was a hit.

Calories per 100 ml of these drinks.Water: No calories, and yet water makes up roughly 60 percent of an adult's body weight.
Calories per 100 ml of these drinks.Black coffee: The brew itself is almost calorie-free, so the milk, sugar and syrup in a cafe order are what add the calories.
Calories per 100 ml of these drinks.Light beer: Light beers mostly cut calories by being lower in alcohol, since alcohol has about 7 calories per gram.
Calories per 100 ml of these drinks.Coca-Cola: Invented in 1886 by pharmacist John Pemberton as a medicine, the early recipe included coca leaf extract and kola nuts.
Calories per 100 ml of these drinks.Whole milk: It's about 3.5 percent fat; skimming away most of that fat cuts the calories by nearly half.
Calories per 100 ml of these drinks.Red wine: Most of the calories come from alcohol, and a standard 125 ml glass delivers around 100 kcal.
Calories per 100 ml of these drinks.Sake: It's brewed more like beer than wine, with mould converting rice starch to sugar, and it is not distilled.
Calories per 100 ml of these drinks.Port: A fortified wine: brandy is added during fermentation to halt it, leaving sweetness; it comes from Portugal's Douro Valley.
Calories per 100 ml of these drinks.Vodka: All its calories come from alcohol, as it contains no sugar, and it's usually bottled at around 40 percent alcohol.
Calories per 100 ml of these drinks.Baileys Irish Cream: This cream liqueur, launched in 1974, blends Irish whiskey with cream, and the sugar and cream make it so rich.

Silk Road stops, by straight-line distan.Lanzhou: The capital of Gansu sits on the Yellow River, and the Silk Road passed through here before squeezing along the Hexi Corridor toward the desert.
Silk Road stops, by straight-line distan.Dunhuang: The cave temples of Mogao near here hold thousands of Buddhist manuscripts, sealed up for centuries and found in 1900.
Silk Road stops, by straight-line distan.Turpan: One of China's lowest and hottest places, this oasis grew grapes and melons using underground irrigation channels called karez.
Silk Road stops, by straight-line distan.Kashgar: The westernmost big oasis in China, where Silk Road routes met after skirting the Taklamakan Desert; its Sunday market is famous.
Silk Road stops, by straight-line distan.Samarkand: The famed city of Central Asia, with its blue-tiled Registan, was Timur's capital, and paper-making reached the West via here.
Silk Road stops, by straight-line distan.Merv: This oasis city in modern Turkmenistan was once among the largest in the world, and is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Silk Road stops, by straight-line distan.Baghdad: The Abbasid capital, founded in 762, was a city of learning, home to the House of Wisdom, where scholars translated Greek texts.
Silk Road stops, by straight-line distan.Antioch: A great trading city in modern Turkey, where eastern goods reached the Roman world; the Acts of the Apostles say believers were first called Christians here.
Silk Road stops, by straight-line distan.Constantinople: Silk reached the empire's eastern capital, and according to tradition monks smuggled silkworm eggs here in hollow canes in the sixth century.
Silk Road stops, by straight-line distan.Rome: The Roman Empire's capital was the far end of the line, and silk was so desired by Romans that senators grumbled about its cost.

Famous books of the Bible, in Bible orde.Genesis: Its name means origin, and it opens with creation, then follows figures such as Noah, Abraham and Joseph.
Famous books of the Bible, in Bible orde.Exodus: Its name means exit; it tells of the escape from Egypt and the giving of the Ten Commandments at Sinai.
Famous books of the Bible, in Bible orde.Psalms: The longest book in the Bible holds 150 songs and prayers, and many are traditionally credited to King David.
Famous books of the Bible, in Bible orde.Proverbs: Much of this book of short sayings is credited to Solomon, and it presents wisdom as a woman calling out in the streets.
Famous books of the Bible, in Bible orde.Isaiah: A nearly complete scroll of this prophet's book was found among the Dead Sea Scrolls and is about 2,000 years old.
Famous books of the Bible, in Bible orde.Daniel: Famous for the lions' den and the writing on the wall, parts of it were written in Aramaic rather than Hebrew.
Famous books of the Bible, in Bible orde.Matthew: This gospel opens the New Testament with a genealogy of Jesus and contains the Sermon on the Mount.
Famous books of the Bible, in Bible orde.John: The fourth gospel differs in style from the first three, and it opens with "In the beginning was the Word."
Famous books of the Bible, in Bible orde.Acts: Traditionally credited to Luke, it follows the early church after Jesus, including Paul's journeys around the Mediterranean.
Famous books of the Bible, in Bible orde.Revelation: The final book is a series of visions, and its name comes from a Greek word meaning unveiling.

Chinese number characters, by value.二: The simplest numeral is two horizontal strokes, and it's the first in a series that grows by adding strokes up to three.
Chinese number characters, by value.四: Four sounds like the word for death in several Chinese dialects, so many buildings skip the fourth floor.
Chinese number characters, by value.五: This numeral is tied to the five elements of Chinese thought, and the number is considered balanced.
Chinese number characters, by value.六: Six sounds like the word for smooth or flowing, so it is considered lucky, especially in business.
Chinese number characters, by value.七: Seven is the number of the Qixi festival, the Chinese Valentine's Day, held on the seventh day of the seventh lunar month.
Chinese number characters, by value.九: Nine sounds like the word for long-lasting, so it's popular at weddings, and it's associated with emperors.
Chinese number characters, by value.十: The character for ten is a simple cross, and it's also used on its own in many contexts as a plus-like sign.
Chinese number characters, by value.百: This character means a hundred, and it also appears in the phrase for all kinds, which literally means hundred kinds.
Chinese number characters, by value.千: The character means a thousand, and the Thousand Character Classic is a poem used to teach children the script.
Chinese number characters, by value.万: This character means ten thousand, and Chinese counting groups numbers in fours, not threes.

Pixar's second decade of films.Toy Story 3: This sequel became the first Pixar movie to gross over a billion dollars, and its furnace scene is a famous tearjerker.
Pixar's second decade of films.Cars 2: Cars 2 was the first Pixar film to get a rotten rating from critics, though it still made over half a billion dollars.
Pixar's second decade of films.Brave: This Scottish fairy tale was Pixar's first with a female lead, and its original director was replaced mid-production.
Pixar's second decade of films.Monsters University: This prequel is set in a monster university, with Mike and Sulley's backstory.
Pixar's second decade of films.Inside Out: Director Pete Docter consulted psychologists to shape how Joy and Sadness handle memory in Riley's mind.
Pixar's second decade of films.Finding Dory: Dory's forgetful quirk in Finding Nemo grew into a full sequel, and the film made over a billion dollars.
Pixar's second decade of films.Coco: The film is set during Mexico's Dia de Muertos, and it won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature.
Pixar's second decade of films.Incredibles 2: The sequel arrived 14 years after the original, and its superhero family returned with Jack-Jack's powers.
Pixar's second decade of films.Turning Red: Pixar's story about a teenage girl who turns into a giant red panda, and it was released directly on Disney+.
Pixar's second decade of films.Elemental: This film set in a city where fire, water, earth and air residents live opened weakly, then leaned on strong word of mouth.

When these cities became national capita.Madrid: Philip II moved his court here in the middle of the Iberian Peninsula; it has been Spain's capital almost ever since.
When these cities became national capita.St. Petersburg: Peter the Great founded it on marshland in 1703; it was the Russian capital until 1918, apart from a brief break.
The government moved from Philadelphia to a new city named for the first president.
When these cities became national capita.Bern: Swiss voters created the modern federal state in 1848; Bern is officially a 'federal city', not a capital.
When these cities became national capita.Tokyo: Edo was renamed Tokyo, 'eastern capital', when Emperor Meiji moved from Kyoto.
When these cities became national capita.Rome: It became the capital after Italian unification, once the Papal States ended in 1870.
When these cities became national capita.Ankara: Ataturk chose this Anatolian town over Istanbul after founding the republic, partly for its central, secure location.
When these cities became national capita.Brasília: A planned city built in about four years; Lucio Costa's layout resembles an airplane, with Niemeyer's buildings.
When these cities became national capita.Abuja: It replaced Lagos as Nigeria's capital, chosen for its central location and designed as a planned city.
When these cities became national capita.Naypyidaw: Myanmar's government moved from Yangon to this purpose-built city, known for its vast, nearly empty highways.

Pregnancies from short to long.Golden hamster: Every pet golden hamster descends from a single wild mother and litter dug up in Syria in 1930.
Pregnancies from short to long.Red kangaroo: The newborn joey is as small as a jellybean, yet crawls unaided into its mother's pouch.
Pregnancies from short to long.Ferret: People have kept ferrets for over 2,000 years, mainly to flush rabbits out of burrows.
Pregnancies from short to long.Gray wolf: Pups are born blind and deaf in a den, and their eyes open after around two weeks.
Pregnancies from short to long.Lion: Cubs are born with faint spots that fade as they grow, and mothers often hide them away for the first weeks.
Pregnancies from short to long.Goat: Goats were among the first animals people domesticated, roughly 10,000 years ago, and twin kids are common.
Pregnancies from short to long.Chimpanzee: It's not far off a human pregnancy, and the baby clings to its mother's belly for its first months.
Pregnancies from short to long.Cow: This lasts almost as long as a human pregnancy, and a single calf is normal.
Pregnancies from short to long.Dromedary camel: A single calf arrives after about thirteen months, and can walk within hours.
Pregnancies from short to long.Orca: Calves are cared for within the pod, and orca grandmothers, which live long after they stop breeding, help the family find food.

Animated TV series premieres.The Flintstones: This prime-time ABC cartoon was modelled on The Honeymooners, and it was first sold as a show for adults.
Animated TV series premieres.The Jetsons: Set in 2062, it ran only 24 episodes originally, and Rosie the robot maid became its most memorable character.
Animated TV series premieres.Scooby-Doo, Where Are You!: Scooby-Doo's name came from a scat line in Frank Sinatra's Strangers in the Night.
Animated TV series premieres.The Smurfs: Belgian cartoonist Peyo created the little blue folk in 1958, and they are famously three apples high.
Animated TV series premieres.The Simpsons: It is the longest-running American animated series, and it began as shorts on The Tracey Ullman Show.
Animated TV series premieres.Rugrats: It was part of Nickelodeon's first Nicktoons trio in 1991, and it was a babies-eye view of the world.
Animated TV series premieres.South Park: Early episodes were made with cut-out construction paper, and in later years each could be completed in about six days.
Animated TV series premieres.SpongeBob SquarePants: Creator Stephen Hillenburg was a marine biologist, and Bikini Bottom is named after the Bikini Atoll nuclear test site.
Animated TV series premieres.Avatar: The Last Airbender: Its world blends Asian and Inuit cultures, and martial arts consultant Sifu Kisu helped shape the bending moves.
Animated TV series premieres.Bluey: The Australian show about a family of dogs is set in Brisbane and is made by Ludo Studio, loved by kids and parents alike.

When these trains first rolled out.Puffing Billy: Built by William Hedley for a Northumberland colliery, it helped prove that smooth iron wheels gripped smooth rails well enough to haul coal.
When these trains first rolled out.Locomotion No. 1: The first locomotive to pull a passenger-carrying public train, on the Stockton and Darlington Railway, built by George Stephenson.
When these trains first rolled out.Stephenson's Rocket: It won the 1829 Rainhill Trials and set the template for steam engines with its multi-tube boiler and angled cylinders.
When these trains first rolled out.The General: Confederate-owned, it was stolen by Union raiders in the 1862 Great Locomotive Chase, a daring Georgia hijack that inspired a Buster Keaton film.
When these trains first rolled out.Flying Scotsman: This LNER locomotive was named for the London-Edinburgh train, and it was the first steam engine officially clocked at 100 mph.
When these trains first rolled out.Mallard: Mallard set the world speed record for steam at 126 mph (203 km/h) in 1938, a record that still stands.
When these trains first rolled out.Union Pacific Big Boy: One of the largest steam locomotives ever built, it hauled freight over the Rockies for Union Pacific, and needed a 4-8-8-4 wheel layout.
When these trains first rolled out.Shinkansen 0 Series: Japan's Bullet Train debuted just before the 1964 Tokyo Olympics and ran at 210 km/h, the world's first high-speed railway.
When these trains first rolled out.TGV Sud-Est: France's TGV set a record for conventional trains at 574.8 km/h in 2007, though the original ran at 260 km/h.
When these trains first rolled out.Eurostar Class 373: Its trains run through the Channel Tunnel, about 50 km long, with roughly 38 km of it under the sea.

Model railway and toy scales.T gauge: Its track is only 3 mm wide, so a complete layout can fit in a briefcase.
Model railway and toy scales.Z scale: Märklin introduced it in 1972, with locomotives smaller than a matchbox.
Model railway and toy scales.N scale: The N stands for nine, since the track is 9 mm wide, and it suits small spaces.
Model railway and toy scales.TT scale: Short for 'Table Top', it was popular in East Germany.
Model railway and toy scales.HO scale: The 'HO' means 'half O', and it is the most popular model railway scale worldwide.
Model railway and toy scales.OO gauge: Used in Britain, it uses HO-width track but bigger trains, to fit Britain's small loading gauge.
Model railway and toy scales.S scale: Famous for American Flyer trains made by A. C. Gilbert.
Model railway and toy scales.O scale (US): Lionel's classic tinplate trains were often sold in this size, a long-time toy-train standard.
Model railway and toy scales.G scale: Large enough to run outdoors in all weathers, it is often called garden railway scale.
Model railway and toy scales.Dollhouse scale: One inch of the model equals a foot of the real thing, the standard among dollhouse miniaturists.

How many different words each one uses.Green Eggs and Ham: Dr. Seuss wrote it on a bet from his publisher that he couldn't do it with only 50 different words.
How many different words each one uses.Toki Pona (language): Created by Sonja Lang in 2001 as a minimalist language to simplify thought.
How many different words each one uses.The Cat in the Hat: Written from a beginner word list of 236 words, it was Seuss's answer to dull school primers.
How many different words each one uses.Basic English (Ogden): C.K. Ogden devised it in the 1920s as a simplified international language, and Churchill promoted it.
How many different words each one uses.Thing Explainer (xkcd): Randall Munroe, creator of xkcd, wrote this book explaining rockets and more using only the thousand most common words.
How many different words each one uses.King James Bible: Its vocabulary is about 12,000 distinct words, yet it shaped countless English idioms.
How many different words each one uses.Shakespeare's complete works: Scholars count about 31,500 distinct words, and he is credited with coining many of them.
How many different words each one uses.Johnson's Dictionary: Samuel Johnson compiled it nearly alone in about nine years, with witty definitions like 'lexicographer: a harmless drudge'.
How many different words each one uses.Webster's 1828 dictionary: Noah Webster's American Dictionary favored American spellings like 'color' and 'center'.
How many different words each one uses.Oxford English Dictionary: A historical dictionary tracing each word's history with quotations, much of it gathered from volunteers' mailed slips.

When these supermarket staples first app.Philadelphia cream cheese: Philadelphia isn't from Philadelphia; the brand's founder chose the name because the city had a reputation for quality dairy.
When these supermarket staples first app.Campbell's condensed soup: Campbell's condensed soup was created by chemist John Dorrance, who condensed it by removing water, and Andy Warhol later made it art.
When these supermarket staples first app.Velveeta: Velveeta was invented in New York and was marketed as a health food at one time because of its whey protein.
When these supermarket staples first app.Wonder Bread: Wonder Bread helped make pre-sliced bread a household norm, though sliced bread arrived in 1928, only a few years before.
When these supermarket staples first app.Kraft Macaroni & Cheese: The boxed dinner's shelf-stable cheese powder became popular during wartime rationing, and cheap meals during the Depression.
When these supermarket staples first app.Cheez Whiz: Cheez Whiz, invented by Kraft, was developed as a spreadable processed cheese, and was originally sold in jars.
When these supermarket staples first app.Pop-Tarts: Pop-Tarts were created to compete with Kellogg's rival Post, which had a similar product on the market, and the frosted flavors became hits.
When these supermarket staples first app.Totino's Pizza Rolls: Jeno Paulucci invented pizza rolls after he dreamed of making a pizza with the form of an egg roll.
When these supermarket staples first app.Hamburger Helper: Hamburger Helper was launched in the early 1970s, when meat was costly, to help stretch ground beef into a meal.
When these supermarket staples first app.Hot Pockets: Hot Pockets were created by brothers Paul and David Merage, and they were first microwaved with a special sleeve to crisp.

When these ad slogans debuted.A Diamond Is Forever: De Beers' campaign by N. W. Ayer helped make diamond engagement rings a standard custom, though few Americans bought them before the 1930s.
When these ad slogans debuted.Melts in your mouth... (M&M's): M&M's candy shell was invented so soldiers could eat chocolate without it melting, and the slogan says it melts in your mouth, not in your hand.
When these ad slogans debuted.Think Small (VW): VW's Beetle ad by Doyle Dane Bernbach turned a small car into a hit in the United States, and its honest style changed advertising forever.
When these ad slogans debuted.We Try Harder (Avis): Avis was number two in rentals, and this honest admission turned its underdog status into a winning campaign against Hertz.
When these ad slogans debuted.Because I'm Worth It: L'Oréal's line was written by copywriter Ilon Specht, who was angry at sexist ads, and it's now a catchphrase.
When these ad slogans debuted.Where's the Beef? (Wendy's): The old lady in the ad, Clara Peller, shouted this line, and it became a political catchphrase after Walter Mondale used it in 1984.
When these ad slogans debuted.Just Do It (Nike): The slogan was reportedly inspired by murderer Gary Gilmore's last words, 'Let's do it', and it helped build Nike into a giant.
When these ad slogans debuted.Got Milk?: The California Milk Processor Board's campaign worked by showing people what happens when you run out of milk.
When these ad slogans debuted.Think Different (Apple): Apple's campaign celebrated rebels like Einstein, and it returned after Steve Jobs came back to the company.
When these ad slogans debuted.I'm Lovin' It (McDonald's): McDonald's slogan was used first in Germany as 'ich liebe es' and then became a global slogan, and it featured Justin Timberlake in a jingle.

How long these lasted.Paris Commune: This radical Paris government declared itself after the Franco-Prussian War and fell during 'Bloody Week'.
How long these lasted.Confederate States: Born to protect slavery, the breakaway states fought the Union from 1861 to 1865 and had no foreign recognition.
How long these lasted.Third Reich: Hitler promised a thousand-year Reich, and it lasted just twelve.
How long these lasted.Berlin Wall: At least 140 people are known to have died trying to cross it, and it fell on 9 November 1989.
How long these lasted.Apartheid: The word is Afrikaans for 'apartness', and the system ended with the 1994 election that made Nelson Mandela president.
How long these lasted.Soviet Union: It lasted from 1922 to its dissolution in December 1991, when the flag over the Kremlin came down.
How long these lasted.British Raj: Direct rule by the Crown began after the 1857 uprising and ended with Indian and Pakistani independence.
How long these lasted.Dutch East India Company: Often called the first multinational, the VOC was also among the first companies to issue publicly traded shares.
How long these lasted.British East India Company: At its peak it ruled much of India with a private army larger than the British Army.
How long these lasted.Romanov dynasty: Russia's last dynasty began in 1613 and ended when Nicholas II abdicated amid revolution.

From a drop to a supertanker.Eyedrop: The tiny volume is often more than the eye's surface can hold, so much of a drop runs down your cheek.
From a drop to a supertanker.Shot glass: The US standard shot of 1.5 fluid ounces equals about 44 ml.
From a drop to a supertanker.Soda can: Cans of diet soda float in water while regular ones sink, because the sugar adds density.
From a drop to a supertanker.Blood in an adult: Your heart pumps all of it around your body in roughly one minute.
From a drop to a supertanker.Elephant's trunkful: The trunk doubles as a snorkel, a hand and a hose, and holds several litres.
From a drop to a supertanker.Bathtub: Archimedes' famous insight about displacement is said to have come in one of these.
From a drop to a supertanker.Hot tub: That is equal to about ten bathtubs, enough to make a large tub heavy enough to need a reinforced floor.
From a drop to a supertanker.Tanker truck: A truck of this size carries roughly 9,000 US gallons of fuel.
From a drop to a supertanker.Olympic pool: The pool measures 50 by 25 metres and at least two metres deep, which equals about 2.5 million litres.
From a drop to a supertanker.Supertanker: Fully laden, one can take miles to stop and is too big for the Suez Canal.

When these medieval Europeans were born.Hildegard of Bingen: This German abbess composed music and wrote about medicine and nature, and she described her religious visions.
When these medieval Europeans were born.Marco Polo: The Venetian merchant's account of Asia was dictated to a fellow prisoner in a Genoese jail.
When these medieval Europeans were born.Dante Alighieri: He wrote the Divine Comedy in Tuscan, not Latin, which helped to turn his dialect into standard Italian.
When these medieval Europeans were born.Petrarch: Called the father of humanism, he wrote sonnets to Laura and is said to have climbed Mont Ventoux for the view.
When these medieval Europeans were born.Geoffrey Chaucer: He wrote The Canterbury Tales in English at a time when French and Latin dominated literature, and worked as a customs official.
When these medieval Europeans were born.Filippo Brunelleschi: He designed the dome of Florence Cathedral without scaffolding and also worked out linear perspective.
When these medieval Europeans were born.Johannes Gutenberg: A goldsmith from Mainz, he printed the famous Bible around 1455 with movable type he cast himself.
When these medieval Europeans were born.Sandro Botticelli: Painter of The Birth of Venus, he was forgotten for centuries before being rediscovered in the 19th century.
When these medieval Europeans were born.Leonardo da Vinci: Left-handed, he wrote his notebooks in mirror script, and he painted the Mona Lisa for years.
When these medieval Europeans were born.Michelangelo: He painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling in about four years, though he always considered himself a sculptor.

When these ships went down.Mary Rose: Henry VIII's flagship sank in the Solent in 1545, and was raised in 1982 and now sits in a museum in Portsmouth.
When these ships went down.Spanish Armada: Many of Spain's ships were wrecked on Scottish and Irish coasts as they fled home around Britain in storms.
When these ships went down.Vasa: The Swedish warship sank within about 1,300 m of its maiden voyage, and was raised in 1961.
When these ships went down.Whydah Gally: It was a pirate ship under Sam Bellamy, and the only authenticated pirate shipwreck ever found, off Cape Cod.
When these ships went down.Titanic: It sank in the North Atlantic with about 1,500 lives lost, and the wreck was found in 1985.
When these ships went down.Lusitania: A German U-boat torpedoed the liner off Ireland, killing about 1,200, and the sinking turned opinion in America.
When these ships went down.Bismarck: It sank HMS Hood days earlier, and its wreck was found by Robert Ballard in 1989.
When these ships went down.Wilhelm Gustloff: The ship carried thousands of refugees and wounded, and is considered the deadliest sinking in history.
When these ships went down.Andrea Doria: It collided in fog with another ship, and most aboard were rescued despite its sinking.
When these ships went down.Edmund Fitzgerald: The ore carrier sank in a Lake Superior storm, inspiring a Gordon Lightfoot ballad.

Germs and parasites that infect people,.Rhinovirus (common cold): Responsible for many colds, it has over 160 types, which is why no single vaccine works.
Germs and parasites that infect people,.Flu virus: Its genome comes in segments that can swap between strains, producing new pandemic versions.
Germs and parasites that infect people,.Smallpox virus: Eradicated in 1980, it is the only human disease wiped out by vaccination; samples remain in two labs.
Germs and parasites that infect people,.Staph bacterium: The name comes from the Greek for a cluster of grapes, and it lives on the skin of many healthy people.
Germs and parasites that infect people,.E. coli bacterium: Most strains are harmless gut residents, and it has been scientists' favorite lab organism for decades.
Germs and parasites that infect people,.Candida yeast cell: A yeast that lives harmlessly on many people, causing thrush when it overgrows.
Germs and parasites that infect people,.Giardia: It clings to the intestinal wall with a suction disk, and is caught from contaminated water, giving it the nickname beaver fever.
Germs and parasites that infect people,.Head louse: It lives only on human scalps, clings with tiny claws and feeds on blood; having it has nothing to do with being unclean.
Germs and parasites that infect people,.Pinworm: Probably the most common worm infection among US children, since females lay eggs near the anus at night.
Germs and parasites that infect people,.Beef tapeworm: Taenia saginata can grow several meters in the gut, absorbing food, and is caught from undercooked beef.

Main CPU clock speed of these consoles.NES: Its Ricoh chip was a variant of the 6502, the same processor family as the Apple II.
Main CPU clock speed of these consoles.Super NES: Slow by comparison, its custom graphics chips did the heavy lifting, including 'Mode 7' scaling and rotating backgrounds.
Main CPU clock speed of these consoles.Sega Genesis: Its Motorola 68000 also powered early Macs, the Amiga and Atari ST; Sega's ads boasted of 'Blast Processing'.
Main CPU clock speed of these consoles.PlayStation: It began life as a Super NES CD add-on that Sony was developing with Nintendo, before Sony went solo.
Main CPU clock speed of these consoles.Nintendo 64: It used cartridges instead of discs, which loaded fast but held little; the '64' refers to its 64-bit processor.
Main CPU clock speed of these consoles.Dreamcast: Sega's last console had a built-in modem, a first for home consoles, letting players go online in 1999.
Main CPU clock speed of these consoles.PlayStation 2: The best-selling console in history, with over 150 million units, its chip was called the Emotion Engine.
Main CPU clock speed of these consoles.GameCube: Its IBM PowerPC chip was nicknamed Gekko, and it played small 8 cm discs instead of standard DVDs.
Main CPU clock speed of these consoles.Xbox: Essentially a PC in a box with a Pentium III-class chip and a built-in hard drive, a rarity then.
Main CPU clock speed of these consoles.Xbox 360: Its three-core IBM chip ran at 3.2 GHz each; the infamous 'red ring of death' hardware fault became its legacy.

Water needed to produce 1 kg of each.Tomatoes: Botanically a fruit, and about 95 percent water itself, yet it is one of the least thirsty crops per kilogram.
Water needed to produce 1 kg of each.Potatoes: Native to the Andes, spuds deliver more calories per litre of water than most crops, which helps explain their staple status.
Water needed to produce 1 kg of each.Apples: Apples float in water because about a quarter of their volume is air.
Water needed to produce 1 kg of each.Bread: Most of bread's water is invisible: it was used growing the wheat, while baking itself uses very little.
Water needed to produce 1 kg of each.Rice: Paddies are flooded to suppress weeds, and flooded rice fields are a notable source of the greenhouse gas methane.
Water needed to produce 1 kg of each.Cheese: It takes roughly ten litres of milk to make a kilo of hard cheese, which is what drives its large footprint.
Water needed to produce 1 kg of each.Chicken: Most of a chicken's footprint is the grain it eats, not the water it drinks.
Water needed to produce 1 kg of each.Pork: A pig eats roughly three kilos of feed for each kilo of weight gained, so most of its water is hidden in its feed.
Water needed to produce 1 kg of each.Beef: Beef tops the common meats because cattle take years to grow and eat a great deal of feed along the way.
Water needed to produce 1 kg of each.Chocolate: Each cocoa pod holds only about 30 to 50 beans, so a bar needs a lot of thirsty trees in the humid tropics.

When these acronyms were coined.ANZAC: Short for Australian and New Zealand Army Corps. It was coined for the 1915 Gallipoli landings, remembered each April 25.
When these acronyms were coined.Radar: Short for RAdio Detection And Ranging, coined by the US Navy in 1940. The British originally called it RDF.
When these acronyms were coined.Scuba: Self-Contained Underwater Breathing Apparatus. It was coined by Christian Lambertsen, who helped develop early rebreathers.
When these acronyms were coined.NASA: Founded in 1958 after the Soviet Sputnik launch, taking over from the older NACA.
When these acronyms were coined.ZIP code: Zone Improvement Plan, introduced by the US Post Office, with a cartoon mascot named Mr. ZIP.
When these acronyms were coined.Taser: Short for Thomas A. Swift's Electric Rifle, from a Tom Swift adventure novel the inventor loved as a boy.
When these acronyms were coined.AIDS: Named by US health officials in 1982. The virus behind it, HIV, was identified the following year.
When these acronyms were coined.GIF: Steve Wilhite created it at CompuServe. He insisted it is pronounced 'jif', though dictionaries accept both.
When these acronyms were coined.JPEG: Short for the Joint Photographic Experts Group, the committee that made photos small enough to share online.
When these acronyms were coined.CAPTCHA: Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart, coined by Luis von Ahn's team at Carnegie Mellon.

Jurassic Park, in story order.Hammond invites the experts: Jurassic Park (1993) is based on Michael Crichton's 1990 novel of the same name.
Jurassic Park, in story order.First sight of a Brachiosaurus: Brachiosaurus lived in the Late Jurassic and weighed tens of tonnes, and the film's one is a landmark moment of CGI.
Jurassic Park, in story order.A baby raptor hatches: The raptors are larger than real Velociraptors, which were roughly turkey-sized and feathered.
Jurassic Park, in story order.Nedry steals the embryos: Nedry hides the embryos inside a fake shaving cream can.
Jurassic Park, in story order.T. rex breaks loose: The T. rex roar was a mix of baby elephant, tiger and alligator sounds.
Jurassic Park, in story order.Sleeping in a treetop: The tree the characters sleep in sits near Brachiosaurus, a dinosaur that could reach high branches.
Jurassic Park, in story order.Ellie restores the power: Ellie Sattler is a paleobotanist, a scientist who studies fossil plants.
Jurassic Park, in story order.Raptors in the kitchen: Real Velociraptors lived in Mongolia and China, not North America.
Jurassic Park, in story order.T. rex takes on the raptors: T. rex had one of the strongest bites of any land animal, and its arrival at the end saves the humans.
Jurassic Park, in story order.Helicopter leaves the island: Spielberg edited the film by satellite link while shooting Schindler's List in Poland.

Treasure Island, in story order.Billy Bones at the Benbow inn: Treasure Island (1883) by Robert Louis Stevenson shaped our image of pirates with its pieces of eight and the parrot on a shoulder.
Treasure Island, in story order.Bones gets the black spot: The black spot is a pirate summons popularised by Stevenson, and it marks a man for death.
Treasure Island, in story order.Jim finds the treasure map: Stevenson drew the map first and then wrote the story to fit it.
Treasure Island, in story order.The Hispaniola sets sail: The ship's name refers to the Caribbean island Hispaniola, now home to Haiti and the Dominican Republic.
Treasure Island, in story order.Jim hides in the apple barrel: Silver's parrot, Captain Flint, squawks Pieces of eight!, which is why parrots are linked with pirates.
Treasure Island, in story order.Landing on the island: Some say Norman Island in the British Virgin Islands inspired Stevenson's setting.
Treasure Island, in story order.Meeting Ben Gunn: Ben Gunn, marooned for years, longs for cheese, a memorable touch of humour.
Treasure Island, in story order.Jim takes the Hispaniola: Jim sails the ship single-handedly, a remarkable feat for a boy.
Treasure Island, in story order.The treasure pit is empty: Real pirates rarely buried treasure, and Captain Kidd is a rare exception.
Treasure Island, in story order.Silver slips away: Long John Silver was modelled on Stevenson's friend W. E. Henley and became the model for later pirates.

Valentine's Day, from saint to swipe.St. Valentine martyred: Legend mixes the stories of at least two early saints named Valentine, and relics linked to him lie in Rome.
Valentine's Day, from saint to swipe.Chaucer links Feb 14 to love: In his poem Parlement of Foules he wrote of birds choosing mates on St. Valentine's Day, possibly the first romantic link.
Valentine's Day, from saint to swipe.Oldest surviving valentine: Charles, Duke of Orleans wrote poems to his wife from the Tower of London after Agincourt; it's in the British Library.
Valentine's Day, from saint to swipe.Penny Post valentine boom: The new cheap postage in Britain, with the Penny Black stamp, sparked a boom in sending valentines.
Valentine's Day, from saint to swipe.Esther Howland's cards: Known as the Mother of the American Valentine, she sold lacy cards from Worcester, Massachusetts, made with imported paper lace.
Valentine's Day, from saint to swipe.Cadbury heart box: Richard Cadbury designed the first heart-shaped box of chocolates, and the boxes were kept as keepsakes.
Valentine's Day, from saint to swipe.Hershey's Kisses: The origin of the name is unclear, but one theory points to the sound of the machine depositing them.
Valentine's Day, from saint to swipe.Hallmark founded: It began with Joyce Hall selling postcards in Kansas City, and a few years later he started selling Valentine's cards.
Valentine's Day, from saint to swipe.Match.com: One of the first major online dating sites, launched when few people had home internet.
Valentine's Day, from saint to swipe.Tinder: It popularised swiping right to like someone, and the app launched at a college party at the University of Southern California.

Chinese dynasties, by founding.Xia: Traditionally China's first dynasty, credited to Yu the Great for taming floods. Archaeologists still debate whether it was a real state.
Chinese dynasties, by founding.Shang: This dynasty left China's earliest written records, questions carved into oracle bones that were cracked with heat to read the answers.
Chinese dynasties, by founding.Zhou: The longest-lasting dynasty in Chinese history introduced the 'Mandate of Heaven', the idea that rulers keep power only while they rule justly.
Chinese dynasties, by founding.Qin: Its first emperor unified China, standardized writing and measures, and was buried with the famous terracotta army of thousands of clay soldiers.
Chinese dynasties, by founding.Han: Founded by a commoner, it opened the Silk Road trade, and many Chinese today still call themselves the 'Han people' after it.
Chinese dynasties, by founding.Tang: A golden age for poetry and trade, its capital Chang'an was one of the world's largest cities, home to merchants from across Asia.
Chinese dynasties, by founding.Song: Under this dynasty came movable type, gunpowder weapons and a navigational compass, plus paper money circulating widely in commerce.
Chinese dynasties, by founding.Yuan: Founded by Kublai Khan, grandson of Genghis, it was the first dynasty to rule all of China from outside the Han people.
Chinese dynasties, by founding.Ming: This dynasty rebuilt much of the Great Wall that tourists visit today and built Beijing's Forbidden City.
Chinese dynasties, by founding.Qing: China's last imperial dynasty, ruled by the Manchu people, required men to wear a braided queue and fell in 1912.
